newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Commercial Bank issue drags Nairobi index.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Commercial Bank issue drags Nairobi index.

text.p: Leading companies made losses at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) on Tuesday as investors moved out to purchase a new primary issue in Kenya Commercial Bank (KCB), brokers and bourse officials said.
They said some of the major losers were Barclays Bank of Kenya and Kenya Breweries, whose performance pulled down the Nairobi stock exchange 20-share index.
The index fell 6.99 points to stand at 3041.62. turnover rose to 37.667 million shillings on 1,120,381 shares compared to 9.573 million shillings on 290,083 shares on Monday.
The Kenyan government, which holds a majority stake in Kenya Commercial Bank, offered for sale on Monday 11.88 million shares or 10 percent of the shareholding at 50 shillings per share.
The government will retain a 60 percent holding in KCB.
The KCB offer was the third in a series of government privatisations through the Nairobi bourse this year. It follows similar ones by Kenya Airways and National Bank of Kenya Ltd.
"The index is bound to maintain this (downward) trend till the end of the month as there is no expected announcement," a broker said.

"Most volumes traded at the general floor were on average, but the turnover was boosted mainly by heavy trading of shares on the three-day special board for Car & General and Kenya Breweries," a Nairobi bourse official said.
Car & General traded a total of 312,824 shares at 21.50 from 21 shillings and Kenya Breweries dealt 440,522 shares at 50 before easing to 45 from 46.50.

Brokers said Kenya Commercial Bank shares were on high demand. "There is good buying of the bank's shares," one said. Most investors are afraid that the may not get the full allotment they have applied for from the primary share issue, where it is cheaper and are turning to the secondary market."
Kenya Commercial Bank traded 13,126 shares at 55.50, 54.50 and 55 from 55.50, National Bank of Kenya rose to 17 from 16.80 while Housing Finance held steady at 25.25 on 92,339 shares.
Among the Plantations, Rea Vipingo rose to 11 from 10.95, Sasini Tea & Coffee fell a shilling to 50 while George Williamson Kenya Ltd eased to 60 from 60.50.
Kenya Airways traded a total of 131,364 shares at 11.20, 10.50 and 10.55 from 11 while Nation Printers & Publishers rose to 105 from 104.
